**Implementation direction (S4.12 only):**

1. **One fixed outcome and complete admission.** Add strict `AllReaders` outcome for the single `summarize` definition, with no read steps, coding target or continuation edge. Forbid it as an edge target under both policies; ordinary `begin`/`execute` cannot launch it. A reader-specific admission takes exactly three borrowed contents, validates each against existing ReaderInputs rules before retaining complete immutable copies (1024 UTF8 bytes/child, LF/TAB permitted, other controls rejected); do not concatenate or use the draft as context. Bind a fresh reader session derived from the opaque command invocation and generation1. Only one initial invocation/one reader owner; validate/copy before dispatch, and initialize the journal with those same complete copies. Host demo fixtures supply disposable contents; no new filesystem reader, arbitrary task count, prompts, discovery or capability mechanism. The journal already owns complete input/root/session/generation binding; do not change its grammar or claim an atomic snapshot of an external checkout.
2. **Actual logical receipt, not public-data authority.** A narrow command reader adapter starts and owns the real ReaderParent against its invocation, inputs and consumed Runtime. Return live ReaderObserver and instance-bound controls, but only the adapter's actual supervisor can mint an opaque one-shot logical execution receipt. Bind shared command-state identity, invocation and actual owner association; no receipt constructor from ReaderTree/ReaderRun/reconstruction/caller labels. Accepting the receipt retains immutable observation, complete child/result/request/usage facts (including siblings after errors) and moves Running to AwaitingCompletion; it does not report success or acknowledge cleanup. Reject foreign/reused/stale receipts, duplicate launch, accept after finalization and omitted/aborted logical execution. A dropped/aborted adapter requests tree cancellation and leaves missing execution/report Incomplete, while the independent owned cleanup path remains available; do not discard the receiver/owner merely because a borrowed wait is cancelled.
3. **Report truth and cancellation ordering.** Command-owned Completed requires the actual correlated logical result, durably acknowledged End, all three children Completed with their matching request IDs and accepted observations, and no command Stop at report acceptance. It means three model summaries were durably accepted, not independently verified conclusions or joined cleanup. With a complete acknowledged tree but any child Failed/Cancelled/NotDispatched, the required AllReaders outcome is Failed; retain every child fact. Missing End, storage/owner failure or unavailable logical result is Incomplete, never a synthesized Failed/success from a partial public snapshot. Explicit command/tree Stop is sticky and wins against both Completed and Failed at the command report mutex; accept Cancelled after the correlated logical outcome, or for a cancelled unlaunched admission. Child-only cancellation goes through the reader control and does not implicitly cancel the command. Late cancellation preserves frozen child facts and already accepted command reports. Failed child facts and uncertain usage remain visible even when the command report is Cancelled. Keep a pre-report AwaitingCompletion marker and a separate explicitly validated bounded ASCII report; receipt acceptance is not reporting. Incomplete is conservative, not permission to invent execution evidence.
4. **Durable completion is distinct from joined settlement.** Existing ReaderParent automatically joins its journal/runtime before returning ReaderRun; add a narrow opt-in command-supervision seam that publishes the logical coordinate outcome after End (or the actual error), then gates journal-thread/runtime joins on the host's settlement release. Preserve existing standalone start/finish/cleanup behavior. The gate is installed before journal/child startup and applies to setup failures as well; no blocking wait or filesystem work under command/bridge locks. The TUI may retain a Completed/Failed/Cancelled/Incomplete logical report while visibly `settled=false`, storage/runtime not joined and fixture accounting unreconciled. Normal Quit, Stop+Quit, signal, watchdog, draw/error and caught-panic paths restore the terminal before releasing the gate, awaiting cleanup, joining the executor, shutting down/reconciling fixture handlers, reconstructing or removing roots. Stop alone requests cancellation and revokes offers; it does not release terminal ownership or pretend to interrupt fsync. Headless callers release settlement without a terminal and await the same actual receipt. Keep the release/cleanup owner outside borrowed logical waits and panic-prone projection code; drop/abandon paths cannot orphan it, self-deadlock a join behind an unreleased gate, or publish settled before actual acknowledgements. Finalization suppresses missing reports but remains unsettled while reader ownership is outstanding. A later join/cleanup failure does not rewrite an accepted logical report; expose the independent failure/unjoined state and retain the disposable root when safe cleanup is not established. No replacement Runtime, resume or second journey.
5. **One combined consumer and bounded host surface.** Implement `command-readers-demo` and opt-in `reader-ui-demo --command`; standalone reader UI remains unchanged. **Implementation direction — one bounded slice, not feature acceptance:**

1. **Command-owned explicit admission.** Add an opaque copyable `CommandResume` with private source invocation identity, available only from a live `CommandSession::paused_continuation()` after an accepted Completed report selected its declared eligible edge. The immutable two-definition catalog and single possible edge make source session/ordinal sufficient identity; no separate generation, random nonce, serialized handle or generic workflow is needed. The getter returns none before the offer, for Pending/Followed/Suppressed/no-edge, cancellation, closure or exhausted slots. Detached snapshots/history are observations, not constructors of execution authority. Add `resume(handle) -> Result<Option<CommandInvocation>, CommandError>` as **admission-only**, analogous to `begin`: validate the current exact Paused source, its accepted report/declared read-only target and free slot under the command state mutex; reject foreign/stale/duplicate/closed handles without allocating or changing facts. A matching handle with cancellation already accepted suppresses that edge and returns none. Otherwise atomically admit fresh invocation2 Ready and record Followed. The host separately calls existing `execute`, observes AwaitingCompletion and explicitly reports the companion. Do not change `follow`'s Automatic-only synchronous behavior or reinterpret declared/host Pause as Automatic. Explicit host calls represent user intent; merely obtaining/copying a handle does not dispatch. Keep schema prohibition on coding edges/targets unchanged.
2. **One fresh painted companion intent.** Replace the binary-private primary-only Offer/latch with two typed cases: initial compare session and command-owned paused resume handle. Retain at most one current offer, one painted offer and one pending intent; consuming either clears current/painted authority immediately. After accepted first report, publish the fresh resume offer only if the command owner supplies it, then wait without holding the command mutex. F5 invokes the current compare or resumes the offered inspect; Enter/paste remain draft input, F3 remains display-tail following, F4 sticky Stop and Quit remain distinct. Show a compact current-action prompt in the visible status area, accepted first report, Paused/unsettled state and keyed source/target identity; final facts remain browseable after companion completion or Stop. New offers require successful eligible painting, flush queued terminal bytes and reset decoder/ingress. Bind split sequences to the offer at their ingress; clear painted authority on focus/Tab changes and inhibit painting/admission while blurred, undersized, resized-away from the displayed geometry or display-exhausted. Old compare bytes, pre-offer/repeated/pasted keys and foreign handles cannot become inspect intent; retain draft/caret/browse/selection across transitions. Existing focus versus editor-focus semantics need no new editing restriction.
3. **Stop and admission linearization, not a blocking bridge.** The executor waits for the exact offered intent on the existing condition variable. When consuming resume intent, hold the bridge mutex only across its sticky Stop check and the **non-I/O** command `resume` admission, then release it before `execute`/reads/report. Bridge→command is the sole nested lock direction; observation/mark/report publication must not hold command state while taking bridge state. This closes the Stop latch→forwarded-control gap: Stop winning the bridge gate admits no companion; command cancellation winning the admission mutex suppresses the edge; admission winning may produce Ready invocation2 but cancellation before its first read dispatch retains zero companion steps. After dispatched reads preserve actual returned facts and separately validate Cancelled/Failed/Completed/Incomplete reporting with existing command rules. First accepted Completed/report is immutable under later Stop. Do not enlarge this slice into changing the existing read-Failed/cancellation report policy; retain actual failure evidence and test it. No retry or replacement after companion failure, lost report or cancellation.
4. **Retained owner and restoration handshake.** Keep the same `CommandSession`/open descriptors/disposable roots in the one blocking executor through the paused wait; observer/control copies do not own roots. After execution finishes, Stop abandons the pause, or an error occurs, keep roots/session until the terminal runner returns from its actual restoration attempt. Add one binary-private terminal-return acknowledgement on the existing condition variable: the outer runner records terminal failure/Stop, acknowledges return on every result path, then joins; only then may the worker finalize and clean roots. Never wait for this acknowledgement while holding a command lock, and Stop alone must not release cleanup while the UI is still active. Logical completion is visibly distinct from `settled`; finalization/cleanup may block only after restoration, and cleanup failure retains root/error truthfully. Ordinary final browsing lasts until Quit or the original sticky30s watchdog/signal/error; no new interval, deadline rearm, runtime replacement or persistence. Successful restoration is demonstrated, not inferred from the acknowledgement; failed restoration is recorded without claiming success or retrying terminal destructors. Uncancelled headless finalization may retain historical Paused+settled with no live handle; Stop/abandonment in the UI suppresses the unexecuted edge. Neither is durable resume authority.
5. **Minimal demos, owners and bounds.** Extend `command-demo` with mutually exclusive `--resume` versus `--automatic`: default stays one report/two reads; --resume obtains the current paused handle, proves no companion read before explicit admission, then executes/reports invocation2 and settles with three reads. In default `command-ui-demo`, host Pause now remains live and F5 offers the one explicit companion; --automatic keeps automatic admission/no companion user offer. Exercise declared Pause under Automatic host through tests, not another CLI policy framework. Primary and companion reread the same exclusively host-owned input root; this is not an atomic snapshot of changing external files. Reuse existing `src/commands.rs`/exports and tests, `src/command_demo.rs`, `src/main.rs`/CLI tests, `src/command_ui_demo.rs`/tests, `src/ui.rs`, `src/ui/command_projection.rs`/resource tests and existing `tests/command_ui_pty.py`/fault helper/Cargo PTY entry. No new dependency/crate, catalog grammar, coding adapter/history/runtime changes or command Markdown. Retain two definitions/two invocations/four reads,1024 bytes/read,4096 catalog bytes,512 aggregate report bytes, two markers, one512-byte error,512-line/32768-byte projection,8192-byte editor,65536-byte frame and200×60 viewport. Meter actual maximum explicit-path parser/admission/snapshot/projection work and rejected-handle allocations; fixed slots do not imply bounded filesystem latency or arbitrary caller clones. README reconciles accepted S4.10 status and accurately states explicit in-memory read-command support and incomplete native/full-S4 readiness. **Implementation direction (one slice, not feature acceptance):**

1. **Validation and authority stay headless-owned.** Extend `src/coding/journal.rs`'s existing strict scan through `src/coding.rs`/`src/lib.rs` with an opt-in immutable supported history result: session/root/version metadata, ordered typed non-header material/effect records keyed by envelope sequence, final operation facts, and a truthful material-ending classification. Keep existing `reconstruct_coding` behavior via the same validation path without collecting material, preserving its allocation baseline; do not create a second permissive decoder. Retain complete material fields and exact Authorized intent fields, not raw serialized journal bytes. Publish nothing until the entire framing/schema/correlation scan succeeds. History carries no CodingProposal/control/approval token and is never input to execution. No schema-version change, repair, import, live snapshot or replay.
2. **Labels report only supported evidence.** Request/Pending is recorded context before admission, with request0, not a dispatched attempt. ResponsePart/Pending is a recorded fragment of settled response material, not an independently durable live-stream receipt; Response/Success acknowledges transport response, not tool/effect success. Tool Error is generic, not proof of denial or cancellation. Final is the recorded validated summary, not a new command completion. Preserve tool-turn versus edit-operation identity and record sequence. Material ending is recorded Final, recorded response Failed, recorded tool Error, or incomplete/no recorded terminal reason (including header-only, complete-line suffixes and exhausted turns). Do not infer interruption cause or fabricate a terminal record. Durable Authorized/NotDispatched/Uncertain/Completed remains a separate effect dimension; readable payloads, live verification, usage and uncertain remote exposure are separately labelled. Validation establishes supported structure/correlation, not independent truth of every payload string; never decode request text into active context or elevate payload claims to authority.
3. **Finite immutable retention before disposable cleanup.** `src/coding_ui_demo.rs` loads once after proven coding-owner termination and lock release, outside the painter/async worker critical path; use the same snapshot's operation facts for existing effect attestation. Publish one shared `Arc` only after validation; retain it through UI exit even after root removal. Keep current target/fixture/live-accounting reconciliation and cleanup error reporting. No load if owner termination is unknown; retain the root as today. Missing/corrupt/truncated/unsupported history has an explicit unavailable error, no partial substitute or live-excerpt fallback. Preserve journal1MiB/64 records/16384 bytes per record/8 operations, material field/turn/response/context caps. Retained decoded string payload ceiling512KiB covers all bounded material/effect fields; reject rather than clip. Selected detail document ceiling32768 encoded ASCII bytes; at most one encoded document cached, plus metadata/current bounded frame. Snapshot cloning shares data; no journal read, all-history encoding or full-history clone per paint. Declare and meter allocation work separately from these payload ceilings.
4. **Explicit non-authoritative history interaction.** Add a coding-only history presentation in `src/ui.rs`/a small private history module: F5 toggle settled history with transcript focus; F6 next fact, F11 previous fact; F9/F10 next/previous512-byte detail page. Bounds clamp fact/page indices; sequence identity remains stable across repaint/focus/resize. Headings distinguish HISTORY READ ONLY from live summary/EXACT EDIT APPROVAL. Use complete reversible printable-ASCII fields (existing encoding convention), explicit source-byte counts/field delimiters and byte-offset gutters; all lines/pages concatenate without inserted bytes. Do not reuse Approval's proposal/coverage/armed state: selected Request can exceed its64-page coverage assumptions. Show unavailable/pending explicitly when F5 precedes a snapshot; never initiate a load or Stop from this key. Current approval takes precedence; history is unavailable while execution is live. Historical F7/F8/F1 do not decide, submit or complete anything. Editor focus retains Unicode/interior paste/editing without resubmission; Tab/browse/follow/resize remain usable. Clear selection/copied state on history entry/exit, fact/page change and terminal reentry; suppress transcript Copy and selection-producing Mouse events while history overlays are shown, avoiding copying the underlying live Display. 5. **Failed-history access must preserve restoration and user Stop.** Successful and denied journeys can settle and expose history inside the existing UI. Real transport/tool failures currently require terminal restoration before owned finish/join: preserve that boundary rather than moving a potentially blocked join into the painter. Distinguish a recoverable coding-failure UI return from deliberate Stop/Quit, signal, watchdog, terminal/input/output and restoration failure. On that recoverable return only: restore terminal, acknowledge restoration, settle/finish and join the executor, then at most once reenter a settled read-only UI with the retained Model/editor/caret/focus and immutable snapshot. **Acceptance boundary:** commands remain immutable outcome/eligible-edge owners; headless execution owns invocation correlation, explicit completion validation, continuation policy and cancellation/settlement. TUI owns terminal presentation and returns intent, never granting capability or treating displayed tool success/final text as command completion. Demonstrate one actual user invocation rather than passive display, auto-start on first paint or per-step CLI subprocesses; reject duplicate/stale intent without extra work. Present bounded safe actual invocation/step/report/continuation facts, including AwaitingCompletion distinct from Completed, default pause and automatic companion requiring its own report; declared Pause remains non-overridable. Preserve failed/unmet outcomes and earlier accepted facts on cancellation, no unrelated substitution/retry, no raw terminal controls and finite byte/work limits. Keep blocking reads off the terminal/async worker; restore terminal before joining owned work on exit/failure, and never claim filesystem deadlines or settlement before dispatched reads return. Retain responsive browsing/editor/focus/resize and existing UI regressions. Planning chooses the minimal meaningful live/final publication and invocation gesture, resolves identities and sizing, and may subdivide if required without widening parent acceptance. Routine automated application/owned-terminal checks remain agent-owned; actual supported-terminal execution must retain candidate/input qualifications, and any foreground desktop input/capture needs separately informed scope/coordination. No new native acceptance follows from headless tests.

**Planning need:** fresh bounded read-only structural mapping and parent source inspection establish accepted synchronous CommandSession execution, cancellation-only cloneable control and snapshot facts, but no command TUI bridge, invocation intent or observer/publication contract. Existing runtime/reader/coding bridges are supporting presentation/lifecycle evidence, not command authorities. Command Paused is a disposition, not resumable execution. **Selected implementation direction (2026-10-26):** one actionable slice, no subdivision or cross-task priority change. Existing design already owns authority and presentation invariants; no new durable product decision or roadmap change is needed. Add binary-private `command-ui-demo [--automatic]` using the accepted disposable `compare`/`inspect` catalog. Default host Pause and opt-in host Automatic remain fixed before invocation; definitions still own eligible edges and outcomes. No resume button, catalog framework, prompt submission, persistence or new dependency.

- **Execution/terminal ownership:** one dedicated blocking executor thread owns setup, the non-cloneable CommandSession, all synchronous reads, explicit report production, optional follow, finalization and exclusively owned fixture teardown. No Tokio task, supervisor/subordinate filesystem thread or per-step subprocess. Check TTY requirements before creating work. Setup may occur before invocation, but discovery/offer/readiness never calls `begin`, `execute` or `follow`. A single wakeable one-shot intent latch (mutex/condition variable or equivalent fixed-capacity primitive) waits for invocation or Stop; do not queue events or grow rejection history. UI/Bridge stop only records sticky intent, wakes the latch and calls the instance-bound cancellation handle; it never reads files, joins or holds a bridge lock across blocking work. Outer run calls UI, receives its actual restoration result, requests Stop and only then joins the executor and emits a bounded safe final receipt. Normal completion can settle naturally while the user browses; exit/failure must restore/attempt restoration before waiting for the thread, even if a dispatched read remains blocked. Restoration failure stays an error. No timeout/detach or filesystem-deadline claim; never declare local settlement/worker join before actual return/join. Panic/error paths preserve available facts, no false completion/cleanup claim, and retain a root if safe teardown cannot be established.
- **One explicit user invocation:** F5 invokes the offered known `compare` command only in this demo; reuse existing F5 decoding mode-locally without changing reader F5 semantics. Enter remains newline, F3 remains display-tail follow, and paste text/embedded key sequences cannot invoke. Offer is bound to the loaded execution session, not an ambient command name: introduce a private offer token from the observer's session identity; the successfully painted current offer supplies input intent. First-paint readiness may enable intent but must not start execution. Focus loss suppresses invocation; stale/foreign tokens, pre-offer intent, repeated keys, invocation after Stop and any second invocation are rejected without more reads/reports/threads. The bridge owns only finite host-intent admission; CommandSession still mints invocation IDs and validates `begin`/execution. Test both latch races and actual terminal input, not merely a direct host call.
- **Minimal read-only publication:** add a cloneable CommandObserver from `CommandSession::observer()` with read-only session identity and `snapshot()` of the existing authoritative state. Keep CommandControl cancellation-only; neither handle can begin/report/follow or alter definitions/facts. Export the narrow observer from `src/lib.rs`; do not migrate commands into HTTP Runtime/coding/readers. All filesystem work remains outside the command-state mutex. The observer survives owner finalization and exposes the same final settled state, avoiding a separate mutable final authority. Bridge holds one observer and cancellation handle for this instance; snapshots are taken without nesting bridge/state locks. The terminal samples one bounded latest snapshot per paint, not per-byte updates. Command phases may be coalesced, but returned step/report/final facts are cumulative and retained. Immediately after each actual execute/follow return and before report, retain one fixed-size keyed pre-report marker (invocation ID, observed AwaitingCompletion phase, reads and returned-step mask), at most two; do not duplicate payloads or infer past phases from final success. Paint these as retained historical observations alongside separately accepted reports. No paint acknowledgement or artificial sleep is needed for completion/continuation authority. This ensures the tiny fast fixture still visibly distinguishes actual AwaitingCompletion from Completed even if live sampling misses it.
- **Completion/policy responsibility:** a binary-private host routine proposes an explicit keyed report from actual facts for this known fixture; CommandSession alone validates the definition outcome, cancellation and eligible edge. TUI cannot synthesize/accept a report, choose a replacement target, override declared Pause or call `follow`. Equal successful reads propose Completed+inspect; mismatched/read-failed inputs propose Failed without next; accepted cancellation proposes Cancelled without next; preserve unexpected failures/missing reports as error/Incomplete rather than invented success. Handle cancellation racing report acceptance by resampling and proposing Cancelled only if cancellation is actually present; no re-execution/effect retry or unrelated fallback. Accepted primary Completed survives later Stop; automatic pending work is suppressed or the actually admitted companion is cancelled, preserving prior reads/report. Each followed companion gets its own observed AwaitingCompletion marker and separately accepted report. F4 requests sticky cancellation while keeping retained facts browseable; Ctrl-Q/signal/UI error exits through restoration-before-join. Stop before invocation means zero invocations/reads. Display host policy and actual Paused/Pending/Followed/Suppressed disposition; no paused-resume interaction.
- **Finite safe presentation:** add command-specific projection with stable IDs keyed by session/invocation/step/chunk, preserved reading anchors and existing draft/focus/selection/resize behavior. Present actual captured contents and source-byte counts, not only success labels; encode reversible ASCII using the existing exact-field encoding convention (literal printable ASCII; quote/backslash escaped; LF/TAB short escapes; other scalars `\\u{HEX}`), with a legend and quoted fields. Do not render raw controls/bidi or truncate semantics. Bound each encoded read to6144 bytes (1024 source bytes ×6), all four read fields to24576 bytes; split into64-byte ASCII chunks (at most96/step) for browseable retained lines. At most512 command lines and32768 bytes of projected line text including names, reports, markers, policy and status; use compact per-read headings and unprefixed64-byte payload chunks, not repeated IDs on every chunk. Maximum read text24576/384 lines + escaped summaries1024/16 + separate worst-case error3072/48 leaves4096 bytes/64 lines for headings/legend/markers/policy/reserved status. Reserve/enforce that capacity and meter the maximum before work claims this limit. Existing65536-byte viewport/copy envelope and editor8192-byte limit remain unchanged. Names/targets/reports retain accepted limits, first error text is bounded to512 bytes, fixed two markers and one intent/error/observer slot; no unbounded caches/queues/history. Authoritative retained read payload remains4096 bytes and summary ceiling512; a sampled snapshot is one bounded disposable clone, not an unrestricted observer-memory/RSS guarantee. Required facts stay retained if terminal is too small to show all at once.

## Accepted task: S4.4

**Outcome/scope:** one offline headless representative command journey discovers one local definition, composes two bounded read-only steps over disposable inputs/owned loopback fixtures, and reports explicit completion with an eligible continuation that either pauses or executes under a declared policy. Current user selected this recommendation in triage session `01a16c99-3247-79e9-9ae3-863e174e54ea`, authorizing planning, local implementation and independent review for this slice only. Preserve existing demos and standalone runtime/coding/readers. No real-project mutation, unrestricted shell, general workflow DAG/DSL/engine, Pi or development-harness compatibility requirement, broad agent/skill catalogs, prompt submission, TUI integration, recovery expansion, real providers, paid/live calls, publication, shared-endpoint load tests, new desktop/clipboard automation or remaining-S4 authority. Planning may subdivide this outcome if sizing demands it; a child acceptance cannot silently finish the parent.

**Acceptance boundary:** command definitions own intended outcomes and eligible continuation relationships; execution validates intent and records correlated facts without becoming a second workflow authority. Discover a bounded local definition and execute two genuinely read-only steps without launching a full CLI per step or requiring a TUI/plugin. Explicit completion is distinct from a model final response, process exit or mere tool success. Demonstrate eligible continuation and pause/automatic policy, reject unknown/invalid/ineligible continuation without substituting unrelated work, and preserve truthful partial completion on cancellation/failure. No success report may grant capability or side-effect authority. Declare limits for definition/input bytes, steps, retained results, discovery and continuation work; prevent unbounded chaining. Preserve existing admission/accounting, exact effect authority and ambiguous-write/no-replay invariants where touched. Planning resolves the smallest concrete fixture journey and checkable completion/continuation contract; do not predesign all command/agent/skill behavior or introduce a new persistent schema without a current necessity.

**Planning need:** fresh bounded read-only mapping and parent source inspection show only static demo CLI dispatch (`src/main.rs:26–39`), prescribed coding context (`src/coding/agent.rs:758–784`) and a terminal-local non-submitting draft; no Rust-product command discovery/composition/completion/continuation contract exists. `.scramjet/rs/commands/` belongs to the development harness, not product implementation or authority. Resolve minimal local-definition trust/capability boundaries, command-versus-executor responsibilities, invocation/result correlation, completion and eligible-edge semantics, pause/automatic policy ownership, cancellation/settlement and finite sizing before choosing files/interfaces. Existing coding final results and reader summaries are evidence/consumers, not implicit command completion. No live provider or native access is needed for this selected headless outcome.

**Selected implementation direction (2026-10-24):** one slice, no subdivision or priority change. Use a deliberately synchronous/blocking headless command executor: definition discovery and sequential finite file reads run on the caller's blocking stack, not a Tokio async worker. No detached task, model request, journal or filesystem-owner thread is needed for this representative journey. Runtime command execution owns validation, invocation facts, completion and continuation; immutable definitions own outcomes/eligible relationships; host intent owns the maximum autonomy. Existing coding/reader final results are not command completion authorities. Ordinary synchronous filesystem latency is not a hard cancellation deadline; any read already dispatched must return before local settlement can be claimed.

- **Concrete journey and discovery:** caller supplies separate explicitly trusted, exclusively owned mode0700 definition and input roots; never change process cwd/environment. Load one fixed local `commands.json`, with at most two command definitions, then discover `compare` by its exact bounded name. Primary `compare` declares two ordered read-basename steps (`left.txt`, `right.txt`) and the `Equal` outcome: both successful byte-exact reads must match. Its sole eligible edge names `inspect`; the companion exists only to prove a real continuation, declares one `left.txt` read and the `Readable` outcome, and has no edge. Equal disposable inputs establish the golden path; differing inputs establish an unmet outcome despite two successful tools. A bounded local two-definition fixture is necessary continuation evidence, not a broad catalog. No ambient/home/ancestor search, directory scan, plugin/prompt discovery or per-step subprocess.
- **Local-definition trust/capability contract:** use a small typed JSON object schema, not development-harness Markdown or a compatibility parser. Declare name, supported outcome, ordered read steps and optional exact next-name/edge policy. Reject unsupported fields/kinds, duplicates, positional arrays, unsupported capability requests, invalid names/step counts/outcome shapes, duplicate definitions, unknown edge targets and cycles before execution. Implement explicit object-only visitors; derived Serde structs alone accept positional arrays. Load and validate once into an immutable per-session snapshot; later on-disk changes do not change an invocation or edge. Definitions are untrusted declarative data: no embedded shell, executable paths, templates, interpolation, model instruction or arbitrary control flow. The only executor capability is a confined file read; no definition, completion or automatic edge grants another capability. This fixture schema is a provisional bounded task mechanism, not a promised public extension/import protocol.
- **Confined file boundary:** retain read-only root descriptors; both definition and input opens are descriptor-relative `RDONLY | NOFOLLOW | NONBLOCK | CLOEXEC`, validate the opened descriptor as regular/single-link, and reject oversized files using metadata plus a fixed cap+1 read buffer. Validate basenames before opening (nonempty ASCII alphanumeric/dot/underscore/hyphen, at most64 bytes, no path components or dot-only names); command names at most32 ASCII alphanumeric/underscore/hyphen bytes. Bound/reject non-UTF8 content and never emit raw terminal controls. No CodingSession/ReaderParent construction: their journals would violate no-write execution. Root permissions and allowlists are fixture isolation, not an OS sandbox or a consistent snapshot of a changing checkout. Captured bytes are the actual read facts; no claim of an atomic multi-file snapshot. Fixture setup/cleanup writes only outside command execution to disposable owned roots.
- **Invocation/completion contract:** mint execution-owned unique session and monotonic invocation identity bound to the loaded definition, roots and ordinal-keyed step facts. Retain settled success/failure/cancellation facts for each actual read. Executing all steps leaves `AwaitingCompletion`, not command success. A separate explicit keyed completion report is required for every invocation, including the companion. Accept `Completed` only when required steps succeeded and the definition's outcome predicate holds; validate any proposed next against that exact source's edge and loaded target. Reject premature, foreign, stale, duplicate, false-success and invalid-next reports without admitting work or substituting a target. Rejection retains the original facts and pending completion; it is not an accepted success or an effect retry. Non-success completion preserves earlier successful reads and suppresses continuation. Cancellation may be claimed only when accepted; missing completion finalizes `Incomplete`, even after successful tools. Final prose/process exit/tool success never substitutes for a report. Reports/facts are in-memory only: no persistence/recovery guarantee or new journal schema.
- **Continuation and cancellation:** edge policy is explicitly `Pause` or `Automatic`; host policy defaults to `Pause`. Automatic execution requires both a declared Automatic edge and host Automatic intent; a declared Pause cannot be overridden by host Automatic. After accepted Completed+eligible-next, retain a correlated Paused target or admit the companion as a new invocation, never fabricate its completion. Pause requires no resume protocol in this slice. An instance-bound control requests sticky tree cancellation; linearize cancellation, result/completion acceptance and next admission through one execution-owned state lock, with blocking reads outside it. Check cancellation before each dispatch and at acceptance; retain a returned read fact even if cancellation prevents accepting completion or starting another step. Completed accepted before late cancellation stays Completed; late cancellation may suppress an unstarted edge or cancel the admitted companion, never rewrite prior facts. Failure/cancellation starts no unrelated work, retry or additional edge. Explicit finalization closes pending completion/continuation and exposes actual settlement; no background operation survives the synchronous owning call.
- **Finite bounds:** one catalog file at most4096 bytes total, two definitions, two read steps/definition, one edge/definition, two invocations and four reads per session including continuation. Each input/result at most1024 bytes, retained read payload total at most4096 bytes; names/identities bounded and step/report storage fixed-capacity. Completion summaries/errors share a512-byte total retained text ceiling per session; format bounded safe output. Reject rather than truncate definition/input/completion semantics; rejected reports add no retained history. Validate limits before copying/allocating caller input, bound parser backing and discovery work, reserve final-status capacity, and refuse continuation at the session ceiling. Finite bytes/operations do not claim bounded filesystem wall-clock latency, arbitrary external observer clones, RSS or node-wide quotas.

**Work surface and acceptance demonstration:** add a headless `src/commands.rs` (only small directly needed parser/support modules if it earns separation), narrow root exports in `src/lib.rs`, binary-private `src/command_demo.rs`, `tests/commands.rs` and focused module-local parser/resource tests. Extend CLI/help/`tests/cli.rs` and affected README with `command-demo` (default pause) and `command-demo --automatic`; preserve existing argument rejection and demos. Do not refactor shared coding/readers/runtime/UI or add dependencies to obtain already available read/parse primitives. The fixture uses synthetic disposable roots; library tests own teardown, and the executable validates/prints actual IDs, step facts, explicit reports, pause/follow disposition and settled local state rather than predetermined success labels.

No new dependencies/features, journal format or reconstruction policy, generic event bus/detail framework, public extension protocol, prompt submission, coding/approval, retry/session replacement or other stage work. Existing design/roadmap invariants already govern this integration; no new durable product decision is needed.

**Headless publication/control contract:** add a reader-owned read-only observation receiver backed by one retained watch state with fixed session/generation identity and three child-indexed slots. Expose no mutable publication sender. Each slot retains actual submitted RequestId, provisional phase/received-byte count (at most2,048; no partial summary), optional accounting receipt, and at most one durably acknowledged ReaderFact with acceptance ordinal1–3. Sender updates mutate only the relevant fields under bounded synchronization; no cloned whole-state-per-delta queue, await/format/I/O under the watch lock, or UI backpressure on persistence/draining. Intermediate progress can coalesce; facts, accounting receipts, errors and final status cannot evict/overwrite prior material facts. Retained accepted summary source is at most3×512bytes, identity64bytes, with error/report backing at most4,096bytes each; preserve existing input3×1,024, response2,048/child, request4,096, storage queue1 and journal32,768 limits. Clone snapshots synchronously at paint opportunities, release borrows before await/format/draw. No observer or slow painter is required for execution.

Publish accepted facts **from the journal owner only after successful Accept append+sync**, before its existing reply. Private `ControlState.accepted` is a cancellation freeze before that write, never a publication receipt. Cancellation before freeze can change disposition; after freeze it cannot revoke completion, even while acknowledgement is pending. Acceptance write/sync failure must publish no accepted fact for that child and retain earlier acknowledged siblings; a physically present record after failed sync is not a live durability acknowledgement. Keep accepted slots immutable and reject duplicate/foreign invocation, child and RequestId updates. Existing early `NotDispatched` children bypass Started/Accept: publish their final facts only after durable End and label them final/not-dispatched, not individually accepted; do not change the journal to manufacture an Accept. Distinguish child acceptance, End/tree completion, storage/runtime joins and failed/unavailable status. A later End/join error does not erase an acknowledged child. Fixed ordinal fields retain out-of-order evidence even when watch revisions coalesce.

Add a small cloned instance-bound reader control handle obtained before consuming `finish`, so the binary can await finish and receive child/tree intent concurrently. It shares the existing cancellation owner, not a second executor. Identity belongs to that instance; bridge projections and intent envelopes carry session/generation and bounded child identity, and validate against the current instance. Actual RequestId remains correlated to submission/terminal/accounting/fact; no retries or child-index reuse in this slice. Preserve existing `cancel_child`/`cancel_tree` callers and parent/drop/aborted-finish tree cancellation. Dropping observation/control clones alone must not cancel a healthy parent. Repeated intent is idempotent; accepted/frozen children preserve existing late-cancel semantics. Control acknowledgement means requested, not accepted Cancelled. Keep closed-watch branches disabled after requesting Stop to prevent a ready-loop spin.

**Accounting correction established by plan review:** accepted ReaderState cannot decide usage/exposure reconciliation. Add one **crate-private runtime-owned receipt query**, using the actual live RequestHandle id after correlated nonduplicate terminal receive and before handle drop. Under the existing state mutex require that exact slot is Complete, and copy independently whether exact-ID terminal-unknown usage and unresolved exposure obligations remain. `State::finish` holds that same mutex through terminal delivery and exposure settlement, so the query sees the completed transition; the still-owned handle retains the slot. Publish this immutable receipt in its separate reader slot before terminal persistence, including actual id, even if later storage/tree settlement fails. Missing/duplicate/foreign terminal or unavailable accounting yields an explicit error/no receipt, never false zero. No generic public Runtime inspection or snapshot reset. The finite demo has no inherited handles/other reconciler/replacement; receipt flags remain stable until its explicit reconciliation. Usage-known/exposure-unresolved and usage-unknown/exposure-settled are independently representable.

ReaderParent already consumes Runtime and shuts it down: preserve that ownership rather than lending Runtime to UI. Await consuming finish **and** the existing cleanup receipt, retaining result errors separately; these establish local/persistence facts, not fixture settlement. Then stop/join the owned listener/handlers and obtain a bounded receipt set keyed by session/generation/child/actual RequestId with declared synthetic final cost1 per captured attempt, including failed/cancelled work. The new fixture returns receipts **without** reconciling; do not adopt legacy ReadersFixture's ignored errors/default usage. For each true runtime receipt bit require an exact matched joined fixture attestation, call the corresponding static usage/exposure reconciliation independently, and fail on unexpected errors. False bits cause no call; missing attestations/receipts retain unknown and fail the settlement expectation. Keep ReaderRun usage and shutdown snapshot historical, not rewritten into successful totals; label the post-attestation process snapshot separately. Successful cleanup proves zero active/pending/handles/backing, joined persistence/runtime/fixture, and explicitly settled exposure/usage/debt while known failed usage stays counted. Reconstruct only after storage lock/thread joins, compare live accepted/final facts without replay, and remove the disposable root only after storage join is established.

**Finite journey and terminal lifecycle:** main thread retains terminal ownership; one ordinary joined thread runs the existing current-thread Tokio executor. Check TTY before starting, start after first successful paint, and route bounded Ready/three-child cancel mask/tree Stop state through a private watch bridge. No worker prints while UI owns terminal. F4 cancels tree; F5 advances selected child cyclically; F6 cancels selected child, supporting SS3 and CSI function-key encodings and ignoring controls while unfocused. Show selected child/invocation, provisional state, accepted summary/disposition, acceptance order, cancellation-request and compact final/join status; the draft never submits. Keep groups/line identities stable by invocation-child-role, preserve displayed selection/anchors and existing control/bidi/grapheme display sanitization. Accepted summaries still need display sanitization: reader text validation does not reject every bidi formatter. Existing frame65,536, draft8,192, retained256 lines, dimensions200×60,64 events/iteration,5ms polling/50ms paint and deadline TTY writer remain unchanged. Make only the small mode-dispatch/safe-text reuse needed by this second concrete consumer; do not generalize the four-request bridge into a framework.

Use a dedicated bounded three-attempt loopback fixture (maximum three accepts, two concurrent handlers,8,192-byte request capture,4,096-byte input) with staged response/durable-publication gates in tests. Interactive success mode releases child1 first, then0/2 with short bounded pacing; stays browsable after completion until explicit exit/watchdog. Three slots are enough: separate deterministic recipes establish all-summary completion, selected-child cancellation leaving siblings completing, tree cancellation preserving an already accepted sibling, failed/malformed/incomplete response and early exit. Do not force every outcome into one three-child run. Assert order from actual durable publication/barriers, not socket receipt order or elapsed host-speed assumptions. Retries0 and fixed ceiling2; request burst4/1ms, synthetic capacity/refill65,536/1ms, cost(1,1), unchanged runtime5s attempt deadline. No adaptive-capacity claim.

On quit/signal/TTY/init/input/draw/write error/panic, request Stop and restore terminal promptly **before** waiting for worker/report completion; always settle owned reader and fixture paths, including init errors. Bound request/terminal draining independently of channel closure: a lost runtime sender/supervisor must not hang the new journey. Allow at most6s after first observed cancellation and35s absolute from Ready for reader transport supervision; expiry records missing terminal/accounting as failure, drops handles and settles remaining children/owner rather than fabricating a fact. Inspect shutdown/owner task failures instead of relying on panic or JoinHandle Drop as joins; fixture shutdown must still run when finish/cleanup errors. Keep the existing30s cancellation watchdog monotonic. **Do not abort/kill the persistence thread or call storage timeout a successful join:** filesystem sync/thread joining is not safely interruptible; demo qualification is an owned regular local filesystem, and tests use finite injected errors/gates. No hard deadline or success guarantee for a hung filesystem. Exceptional unjoined/unavailable cleanup must remain a failed, explicitly qualified result; successful normal and injected ordinary-failure journeys require actual joins. Avoid root deletion/executor teardown being presented as proof of storage/runtime settlement. Reuse deadline post-restoration report/error output and error aggregation; terminal restoration must not depend on a successful async join.

**File direction:** reader-owned observation/control/accounting surface in `src/readers.rs` (a private reader submodule only if size warrants) and explicit `src/lib.rs` exports; exact runtime receipt query in `src/runtime.rs`; affected deterministic reader/runtime tests in their existing modules and `tests/readers.rs`, `tests/readers_exposure.rs`, `tests/readers_meter.rs`. Binary-private `src/reader_ui_demo.rs` owns bridge/finite orchestration; private `src/ui/reader_projection.rs`, `src/ui.rs` and `src/ui/input.rs` own presentation/mode/intent, reusing only the concrete safe-display/terminal pieces needed from existing request mode. Register CLI in `src/main.rs`/`tests/cli.rs`. New dedicated `tests/support/reader_ui_fixture.rs` and reader PTY script keep legacy fixture/request journeys unchanged; integrate via `tests/ui_terminal.rs`. Adapt the native wrapper narrowly for reader mode without weakening existing request checks. README records truthful controls/status/receipt qualifications; progress records candidate/checks. Manifest/lock/notices, journal format, command definitions, design/roadmap and unrelated dirty/sibling files are not planned changes.

**Hard ceiling/effective target:** add one explicit fifth constructor argument, exported `ConcurrencyMode::{Fixed, Adaptive}`. Existing callers explicitly select Fixed; the new journey selects both modes. `active_limit` remains the immutable validated1–4 hard ceiling and `ReaderParent`'s configured-ceiling2 contract remains unchanged. Adaptive starts at that ceiling, floors at1 and never exceeds it; Fixed always targets the ceiling. The common mutex-ordered `can_start` and `timing_wait` use the effective target for active-slot eligibility without relaxing any FIFO/request/token/cooldown/exposure/usage/byte gate. A decrease grandfathers all committed Starting/Running attempts, including not-yet-dispatched ones: no revocation, refund, requeue, retry or channel/accounting change. An increase wakes the same supervisor. Adaptation has no periodic task/Sleep: existing timing gates and completion/feedback notifications suffice. Cancellation/shutdown do not wait for adaptive recovery. A stopped clean owner may be replaced under all existing independent guards; the old target itself is neither a new replacement blocker nor permission to clear obligations. A new clean owner starts at its declared mode/ceiling; live owner mode/target cannot be reset externally.

**Pressure and damping:** correlate observed HTTP status with the live RequestId under the state mutex at the existing response-head checkpoint, before teardown and later admission. 429 is a refusal observation whether Retry-After is valid/missing/invalid; retain its exact metadata and existing cooldown rules. 502/504 are a separate proxy-pressure class and never create cooldown or claim rate limiting. These classes can decrease target even without synthetic usage evidence; they cannot erase exposure/unknown usage. Every observed pressure resets recovery samples and records last-pressure time. Decrease to `max(1, ceil(target/2))` at most once per250ms; the first pressure may decrease immediately, subsequent pressure inside that interval records pressure but cannot decrease again. Record last actual decrease separately from last pressure so repeated observations cannot accidentally extend/deactivate the decrease guard. Pressure at floor1 still resets recovery. Other statuses, deadline, transport uncertainty, cancellation, framing/local resource failures and consumer loss are excluded, explicitly counted by class, not relabeled rate-limit or proxy evidence. They reset a partial recovery streak but do not themselves lower target. Late pressure from a grandfathered committed attempt is still observed pressure and obeys the guard; late success must not raise a newer target.

**Qualified recovery/sample bounds:** use only a clean protocol Success after runtime usage/overrun qualification, with Known synthetic final usage, no output-channel backpressure, and a fresh demand-backed commitment witness from the current target generation. At commitment, record a demand flag only when the resulting active count reaches the target and a remaining FIFO head could otherwise commit: head exists, request credit and that head's token credit/debt permit it, cooldown absent, exposure and usage each have room. Do not infer demand from fixture receipts or later queue/active samples. Immediate submits with no queued head lack this witness. Capture target-generation identity and commitment time in the existing bounded slot; each actual target change advances generation without wrapping into an old identity. Stale-generation or older-than2s successes cannot grow target. Four consecutive qualified samples, each after at least250ms without observed pressure and with no gap above2s between samples, raise target by exactly1, then clear the streak and advance generation. Ineligible/non-success completions reset the streak; no history persists across changed targets. At the ceiling, do not accumulate future growth credit. Unknown usage, credit/exposure saturation, sparse demand and a slow consumer are not capacity evidence. Time passing alone never grows target. Fixed collects diagnostics but never changes target.

Bound controller state to scalars (target, generation, timestamps, streak≤4, last change reason) plus per-live-slot scalar witnesses; no rolling unbounded observation/event vector. Checked cumulative counters/generation must never wrap or fabricate exact history; on generation exhaustion disable growth conservatively until clean replacement. Snapshot adds mode/ceiling/target, recovery sample count, observed class counts, decrease/increase counts and last transition time/reason; overflowed cumulative diagnostics become explicitly unavailable. Existing commitments remain the authoritative per-handle history. HTTP adds a scalar dispatch-to-response-head duration and backpressure flag to its private attempt result/slot evidence; expose bounded diagnostic timing as needed in Terminal, never use elapsed time as a pressure threshold. Header latency excludes queue/pacing/cooldown/connect and downstream output waits but is still client/proxy/transport latency, not backend service time or TTFT. Report total commitment-to-terminal latency separately. Test unsuccessful/missing header timing as absent, not zero; no header maps/clones/new response protocol or changed byte/context/output maxima.

## Accepted task: S3.4

**Outcome:** every implemented model attempt uses one explicit fixed process-local synthetic token budget under the runtime admission owner, with bounded reservation/accounting and truthful known/unknown usage. One observable owned-fixture journey, not real provider token support.

**Scope/non-goals:** user selected this option after fixed token-budget/adaptive/stop/other alternatives on 2026-10-09. Authorization covers one bounded offline slice through planning, implementation and independent review. Runtime remains admission/cancellation/exposure authority; HTTP supplies qualified synthetic protocol evidence; coding/readers remain consumers. No byte-to-token claim, real tokenizer/model context/output maxima, provider billing/limits, adaptive concurrency, retries/compaction, generic quota controller/SDK, cross-process sharing, live/paid calls, publication, native replay, runtime/TUI integration or remaining-S3 work.

**Acceptance boundary:** plan declares synthetic cost units and trusted cost/usage source, bounded budget/configuration, burst/refill and reservation/charge/reconciliation events. Both immediate submit and FIFO promotion obey the same mutex-ordered policy; all model consumers participate without reducing existing context/output byte bounds. Distinguish estimates/allowances from evidenced synthetic actual usage and unknown failed/cancelled usage; no fabricated zero, double counting or premature refund. Resolve oversized/overrun costs, unknown obligations, replacement exclusion and the limited recovery/reconstruction claim before implementation. Preserve request pacing, cooldown, exposure, cancellation, FIFO, bounded queued/backing/timer state, successful-response gating and exact-effect/no-replay history. Use explicit clock/barrier accounting tests plus actual owned HTTP coding/reader journeys, failure/cancellation/unknown usage challenges and joined cleanup; report workload/host/candidate/timing/occupancy without provider/node/backend capacity claims. Preserve normal Rust checks and current demos; authenticate unchanged dependency/notices inputs or audit changes. Independent acceptance required for shared budget/usage/admission and persistence/cancellation contracts.

**Planning need (resolved below):** current runtime `submit(&str)` bounds 4,096 bytes but has no token-cost contract; Terminal contains byte counts and Retry-After, not usage. Coding/reader `usage_tokens` are currently `None`; that unknown must not silently become measured tokens. Fresh bounded read-only structural mapping and parent source inspection establish runtime as the shared owner, common commitment boundary, subordinate HTTP and existing completed-response consumers. Cost qualification, reservation versus actual/unknown obligations, usage attribution and recovery semantics required the plan below. The resolved slice keeps conservative nonrefundable reservation charges distinct from measured synthetic usage, retains bounded unknown obligations independently of exposure and makes no durable token-recovery claim. No adaptive controller or provider values are selected.

**Plan (2026-10-09):** one implementation slice, no subdivision or priority change. Runtime owns admission, reservation/charge, retained usage obligations and replacement exclusion. HTTP only supplies bounded qualified synthetic protocol evidence; coding/readers are consumers. Keep usage obligations separate from remote exposure: observed refusal can settle exposure without known usage, and fixture exposure attestation cannot erase usage uncertainty. No new dependency, public clock/reset hook, generic quota controller or journal format is needed.

**Synthetic cost/configuration contract:** add an explicit fourth `Runtime::new` argument, exported validated `SyntheticTokenBudget` with private fields: capacity **1–65,536 units**, refill quantum **1–capacity units per interval**, interval **1ms–86,400s inclusive**, preserving fractional Duration. Add exported validated `SyntheticCost` with two explicit input/output allowances, each **0–65,536**, checked nonzero total; `submit(input, cost)` rejects total above the configured capacity before allocating identity/channels/input backing. These are caller-declared synthetic allowances, not estimates derived from byte lengths, real model context/output maxima or billable tokens. Every direct and indirect model attempt must supply a cost; no implicit unmetered/default constructor or submit overload. Keep all existing byte/context/output bounds. Tests/old demos explicitly use capacity65,536, quantum65,536/1ms and cost(1,1), unless exercising a declared budget; coding/readers use explicit fixed cost(1,1) per turn/child. The new demonstration declares its smaller budget. Do not copy caller-provided cost fields from untrusted response content.

**Reservation/charge and refill:** under the existing state mutex, admission commitment consumes reservation **R=input+output allowance** exactly once, alongside the existing request-rate charge and exposure reservation. Pending requests hold a cost scalar, not budget credits. Both immediate submit and FIFO head promotion require credit≥R, zero overrun debt, usage-obligation room, absent cooldown and existing active/exposure room; no smaller-cost tail bypass. Pending/rejected work charges nothing. After commitment there is **no refund**, including undispatched cancellation, connection failure, known actual<R or known zero: reservations are conservative admission charges, never labeled measured actual usage. Valid actual A>R additionally charges **A−R**, subtracting current credit first and recording remainder as scalar debt; no double charge on reconciliation. Existing committed attempts are grandfathered, not retried/requeued. Valid overrun cannot drive tools/successful summaries: otherwise successful terminal becomes `ResourceLimit`; preserve an already failed outcome while still accounting known actual.

Use a small private fixed-state token bucket, not a generalized rewrite of the request-rate bucket. Initially full. Each whole monotonic interval earns one quantum; earned units pay debt first, then refill credit capped at capacity. While debt>0 no new commitment; no refund event replenishes credit. On becoming/already fully replenished with zero debt, discard surplus elapsed time and reset phase to refresh time. Before full, retain fractional elapsed remainder. Arithmetic is constant-work u128 elapsed division, comparison against bounded missing-credit+debt before multiplication/narrowing, and checked bounded scalar updates. At most four committed usage obligations coexist; each actual≤65,536 and new commitments stop on debt, so enforce/verify conservative debt≤**4×65,536**. Compute the FIFO head's wait from debt plus missing head credit, rounded up to whole quanta minus retained remainder. Extend the single supervisor Sleep to max(cooldown, request-rate wait, head token-cost wait), retaining checked≤day chunks and notifications. Unknown-obligation/active/exposure-only blocking must not spin or manufacture a timer; cancellation/shutdown never waits for credit/debt recovery.

**Usage evidence and bounded obligations:** create a fixed-capacity≤4 usage record keyed by RequestId at commitment, independent of slot/lease/exposure lifetime. Terminal carries an exported scalar synthetic-usage enum: `NotAttempted`, `Unknown`, or `Known(total)`; naming/docs must qualify it as synthetic. NotAttempted requires no conservative dispatch marker (including queued cancellation), does not claim remote billing zero and does not refund a commitment. Dispatched failure/cancellation/missing or untrusted evidence is Unknown, never zero. Known means only trusted fixture final evidence, not successful tool/schema execution. On local finish, Known charges excess then removes the usage record; NotAttempted removes it; Unknown remains after handle destruction and can occupy all four entries. Time/refill/exposure reconciliation does not remove unknown records or prove their final cost. At four records, pause commitments even when token credit and remote-exposure room return; pending/backing limits remain unchanged.

Define a second explicit process-static one-shot `reconcile_usage_fixture(id, actual)` for fixture-owner attestation of **final** synthetic actual≤65,536 after locally terminal Unknown; reject active, absent, duplicate or invalid attestations without mutation. It charges excess exactly once, removes only that usage obligation and wakes the supervisor; it does not settle remote exposure. Keep existing `reconcile_fixture(id)` solely for its correlated exposure attestation. No automatic zero attestations, expiry, force reset or stale-id forgiveness. Test fixtures may declare exact synthetic final cost in advance and attest it after their joined final observation, but socket close alone is not usage evidence. Add bounded snapshot config/credit/debt/obligation counts/known measured total and conservative charge totals; checked cumulative-total overflow becomes explicitly unavailable, never wraps or silently saturates into an exact measurement. RequestIds retained for obligations are bounded, not a growing history.

**HTTP evidence contract:** send no byte-to-token estimate. Owned fixtures may return exactly one `X-Fixture-Usage-Id` header matching this attempt's RequestId and exactly one `X-Fixture-Usage-Tokens` final total **0–65,536**. Strict borrowed ASCII decimal parsing, no signs/whitespace/comma lists; length≤20 for id and≤5 for usage, checked arithmetic, exact id match. No header clones/maps/history or relaxed existing 16-header/4,096-head/wire/body bounds. Both absent means Unknown; one missing, duplicate, malformed, out-of-range or mismatched evidence is invalid/Unknown and disqualifies otherwise-successful completion (`Framing`). Still preserve Retry-After feedback and observed non200 exposure settlement; an already failed HTTP outcome remains failed. A success-head candidate becomes Known only after valid DONE plus clean body EOF within deadline; partial framing, cancellation/deadline/consumer loss/resource/transport failure leaves Unknown even if its header parsed. For an observed non200 fixture response, this explicit synthetic protocol declares those head values final refusal usage, so valid evidence is Known despite failure; this is not a claim about real provider headers. Invalid metadata never becomes model text/tool arguments. No trailers or in-stream usage-schema extension.

**Consumers and recovery limit:** propagate correlated terminal usage into live coding/readers results; known run total only when every attempted turn/child has known evidence (NotAttempted is not an unknown dispatched cost), using checked sums. A mixed run remains unknown, and known failed work remains in runtime accounting even when a consumer returns Err or rejects schema/tools. Do not collapse unknown child usage into zero or recursively copy histories. Existing `usage_tokens: Option<u64>` may remain for this bounded live aggregate but must be documented as synthetic, not real provider measurement. Do **not** add durable usage records or change coding/reader journal versions in this slice: restart reconstructs existing effect/reader facts only; no usage total or active reservation is reconstructed. Process restart loses synthetic budget authority and is not live-provider recovery. Existing reconstruction stays read-only/no replay; interrupted/dispatched work remains uncertain. No new resume execution path. This explicit limited recovery claim resolves S3.4's boundary without a persistence framework.

**Replacement:** keep process-static retained owner. A replacement requires no usage records, zero debt, fully replenished synthetic and request-rate buckets, plus all prior stopped/slot/reference/cooldown/exposure guards. Full credit alone is insufficient while usage is unknown. Config/endpoint/ceiling changes cannot erase live obligations. Post-shutdown process-static usage/exposure attestation and natural refill permit replacement only after all independent guards hold. No public reset/update API; process restart is outside enforcement/recovery claims.

## Accepted task: S3.3

**Outcome:** every implemented model attempt shares one explicit synthetic fixed request-rate budget under the process-local admission owner; queued work progresses at the declared rate without bypassing accepted cooldown, active/exposure ceilings or cancellation.

**Scope/non-goals:** one offline slice using owned loopback fixtures and bounded requests/state/timers. Runtime remains admission/cancellation/exposure authority; HTTP supplies protocol evidence; coding/readers remain consumers, not independent budget owners. No token estimation/accounting/pacing, adaptive concurrency, retries/compaction, real provider limits/authentication, generic quota-pool SDK/controller, cross-process/tab coordination, native replay, runtime/TUI integration, publication or remaining-S3 authority.

**Acceptance boundary:** planning must declare the fixed synthetic budget, supported configuration bounds, burst/window/spacing semantics and the precise charged attempt event. Both immediate submit and queued promotion obey one mutex-ordered policy. Distinguish commitment, actual send and fixture receipt; define cancellation before/after charging and failure accounting without replenishment that could bypass the budget. **Plan (2026-10-09):** one implementation slice, no subdivision or priority change. Runtime remains the essential admission/accounting/cancellation/exposure authority; HTTP remains subordinate protocol/transport evidence, coding/readers remain consumers, and fixtures/demo supply stimuli and measurements. Use one small private fixed-size discrete token bucket in existing runtime state; no dependency, production clock trait, generic quota identity/controller, refill task or timer per waiter. Existing approval, durable codecs, reader acceptance and remote-settlement policy remain unchanged.

**Explicit budget/configuration:** require a third `Runtime::new` argument: a concrete exported validated `RequestRate` value with private fields, burst integer **1–4** and refill interval **1 millisecond–86,400 seconds inclusive** (Duration may contain finer fractional units inside those bounds). Its constructor rejects invalid values before runtime construction/state allocation; no unpaced constructor, implicit default, zero/infinite rate, provider-derived values, reset/update API or compatibility overload. The synthetic demonstration uses **burst2, one token/250ms (4 commitments/s sustained)** with active ceiling2. Existing fixture/demo/test consumers explicitly choose **burst4/1ms** unless testing a different declared rate; this is a test budget, not verified provider capacity. All implemented model attempts necessarily use a configured owner. Constructor migration includes every repository consumer (102 current call sites); preserve their assertions, adapting timing/control only where pacing genuinely changes behavior. No general configuration struct or new crate hierarchy is needed.

**Burst/refill semantics:** initially full; one commitment consumes one whole token. While below burst, earn one token per full monotonic interval, retain fractional elapsed time, and cap at burst. On reaching/already being full, discard surplus elapsed time and reset the refill checkpoint to the refresh instant; idle time cannot bank an extra burst or old phase for an immediate bonus token after draining. This is a discrete token-bucket envelope, **not** a rolling-window quota or strict inter-request spacing: up to burst commitments can coincide, and fractional remainder near a refill boundary can allow a subsequent commitment soon afterward. Arithmetic uses monotonic elapsed Duration/u128 nanoseconds, caps earned tokens against ≤4 missing slots before narrowing, and avoids multiplying a huge elapsed interval count or constructing a far-future deadline. Remainder is less than the bounded interval. Fixed scalars only: config, available tokens and monotonic checkpoint; refresh is constant work regardless of idle duration. Do not silently round configuration to integer milliseconds or shorten waits; Tokio tick rounding may delay wake, never authorize early commitment.

**Charge and linearization:** `State::start` under the existing state mutex charges exactly once at the **admission commitment**, alongside active/exposure reservation and the existing commitment counter. Both immediate submit and FIFO promotion refresh/check the same policy before this charge. Input/Full/Shutdown rejection and cancellation of Pending work charge nothing. Once committed, cancellation before actual send, connection failure, refusal429, protocol/transport failure, deadline, success and handle drop **never refund**; earned tokens depend only on elapsed time, not outcome or exposure settlement. A charge remains consumed even if the committed attempt never sends. Cancellation that wins before promotion avoids charging; commitment ordered first consumes a token and follows the existing Starting/Running cancellation path. Preserve the five-second attempt deadline beginning at commitment, not queue arrival. Do not insert a second pacing delay inside HTTP, abort/requeue grandfathered commitments or retry failures.

The budget bounds **commitment events**, not socket writes/receipt timestamps. `Shared::dispatched` is a conservative marker immediately before `send_request`, not successful-byte transmission. A delayed committed attempt can send later alongside other previously committed work; accepted cooldown grandfathering also permits this. At most the active ceiling bounds this set. Record commitments, conservative dispatch counts and full-request fixture receipts separately; never infer FIFO or strict spacing from concurrent socket arrival or claim endpoint/node/provider quota enforcement from this process-local envelope.

**Timing/cooldown/exposure:** keep one optional supervisor Sleep. After refreshing timing under the mutex, pending promotion requires rate token, absent cooldown, active room and exposure room simultaneously. For pending work, a finite positive timing obstruction wakes after **max(cooldown remaining, next-token wait)**, using the existing checked ≤one-day chunks. An indefinite cooldown has no expiry timer. If timing is already eligible but exposure/active occupancy blocks, wait for existing notifications/task joins, not a zero-duration Sleep loop. A timing wake only rechecks eligibility; it never clears exposure or grants exposure credits. Preserve notified-before-lock and queued-cancellation-before-promotion ordering. Tokens may refill during cooldown, but only up to burst; expiry can allow that declared burst, not a cooldown-sized catch-up queue. Overlapping Retry-After retains max-not-add behavior; earlier commitments remain grandfathered. Cancellation/shutdown/drop process queued work promptly without waiting for either timing debt to expire; cleanup still requires a driven executor. Use fixed scalar snapshot diagnostics for declared rate, available tokens, next-token and full-refill remaining durations, and last commitment monotonic instant if needed to measure actual commitment timing; no timestamp history/header/map or public injection API.

**Owner replacement:** retain the existing process-static owner after shutdown/drop. Refresh its bucket under process-owner→state lock order. Replacement returns `RuntimeBusy` while the old bucket is **not fully replenished**, even if one token would permit a request, plus all current cooldown/stopped/slot/exposure/reference conditions. Waiting only for the next token would allow repeated owners to reset to fresh bursts. Natural full refill and all prior obligations gone permit clean replacement with a new endpoint/ceiling/rate; the full old capacity is then equivalent to a replenished owner, not a live-debt reset. No early manual reset or mutable rate bypass. Time/full refill never settles unresolved RequestIds. Process restart does not persist this synthetic budget/exposure authority and is not live-provider recovery.
